title: the chakras as a map, not a claim (science seat)
hook: a rainbow poster says yellow; the old text says the color of a rain cloud

segments.voice: Yesterday, the chakras as a map, and its lines: Ida with the moon, Pingala with the sun, and one map with two ways to hand it on. Today, its colors.
screen: `ONE MAP, TWO WAYS TO HAND IT ON.`

segments.voice: On a yoga studio wall there's a poster: circles stacked up a seated figure, red at the base, then orange, then yellow at the navel, on up to violet at the crown. A neat rainbow, easy to remember. Now open the Sat-Cakra-Nirupana to the lotus at the navel. It isn't yellow. The text says it's the color of a heavy rain cloud: dark, full, about to break.
screen: `A RAINBOW ON THE STUDIO WALL.` → `YELLOW AT THE NAVEL.` → `THE OLD TEXT: A RAIN CLOUD.`

segments.voice: The text calls this lotus Manipura. So which picture is right? That's the science seat's favorite question, because the answer is the whole lesson. The old text paints each lotus its own way: its colors, its letters, its shape, its seed sound. The colors aren't lined up like light through a prism. They belong to a picture the meditator builds, detail by detail. The rainbow poster comes from somewhere else. It's tidy and easy to print, and it may help someone too. But it isn't the old text's palette. Here's the turn. If the chakras were organs, two pictures this different would mean one was simply wrong, the way two X-rays of the same knee can't both be right. Maps work differently. A street map and a subway map of one city disagree all the time, about distances, about colors, about what's even shown, and both get people home. When two maps of the same ground disagree, it's a clue that they're maps: drawn by someone, for a purpose. So the honest move isn't to pick a winner. Ask each map what it's for. The poster helps a beginner remember an order. The old text builds a world for the mind to rest in, rain cloud and all.
screen: `THE POSTER: A RAINBOW.` · `THE OLD TEXT: A RAIN CLOUD.` · `TWO MAPS CAN DISAGREE.` · `ASK EACH MAP WHAT IT'S FOR.` · then, large: `RAIN CLOUD AND ALL.`

segments.voice: Find one dark, deep color near you: the shadow under a chair, a navy shirt, the gray of a cloudy window. Let your eyes rest in it for the whole sit, noticing the shades hiding inside one color. When your mind reaches for a label, come back to just looking.
The chakras as a map: at the navel, Manipura, the color of a heavy rain cloud in the old text, not the yellow of the poster.
screen: `THE CHAKRAS AS A MAP — today's word`.

segments.voice: Hold on to this: the chakras as a map, not a claim, and two maps can both be useful. That's day sixteen forty-nine.

screen: `DAY 1649 COUNTS.` → `THE TANTRAS, FRAMED · 41 OF 42.` → `TOMORROW: THE TOP ISN'T THE END. WHERE NEXT?`
